q: Batteries and generators are called sources of _____ force.
e: Batteries and generators are sources of electromotive force.

q: A battery converts _____ energy into electrical energy to provide electrical power.
e: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

q: In an electric generator, _____ energy is converted into electrical energy.
e: In an electric generator, mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy.

q: The main function of the source is to send negative charges from the positive terminal to the _____ terminal within the source.
e: The main function is to send negative charges from the positive to the negative terminal.

q: Electromotive force is the amount of energy provided by the battery per unit charge to move round the _____ circuit.
e: Electromotive force is the energy per unit charge to move round the complete circuit.

q: The unit of electromotive force is volt, equivalent to _____ per coulomb of electric charge.
e: Volt is equivalent to joule per coulomb ($J C^{-1}$).

q: Despite its name, electromotive force is not actually a _____.
e: Despite its name, electromotive force is not actually a force.

q: The internal resistance of a battery depends on its size, chemical properties, life time, and _____.
e: Internal resistance depends on size, chemical properties, life time, and temperature.

q: A battery which has an internal resistance $r$ must be viewed as having a resistor of resistance $r$ connected in _____ to the battery.
e: The internal resistance is regarded as being connected in series to the battery.

q: The equation $E = IR + Ir$ is called the _____ equation.
e: The equation $E = IR + Ir$ is called the circuit equation.

q: The potential difference across the terminals of a battery connected to an external circuit is called the _____ voltage.
e: It is called the terminal voltage or available voltage.

q: Electromotive force (emf) is the potential difference between the two terminals of a battery in an _____ circuit.
e: Emf is the potential difference in an open circuit when no current flows.

q: Terminal voltage is the potential difference between the two terminals of a battery in a _____ circuit.
e: Terminal voltage is the potential difference in a closed circuit.

q: When a battery having an internal resistance is used in an electric circuit, the potential difference between the terminals is always _____ than its emf.
e: The terminal potential difference is always less than its emf when discharging.

q: When charging a battery, the potential difference between the terminals is equal to _____.
e: When charging, the potential difference is $V = E + Ir$.

q: The potential difference or voltage is the amount of energy required to move a unit charge from one end to another end of a circuit _____.
e: Voltage is the energy required to move a unit charge across a circuit element.

q: In charging a battery, the chemical energy which has been used up is supplied back by _____ energy from some external source.
e: Chemical energy used up is supplied back by electrical energy during charging.

q: A steady current will flow through the conductor if a steady _____ difference is maintained between its ends.
e: A steady current flows if a steady potential difference is maintained.

q: The positive charges are sent from the negative terminal to the _____ terminal within the source.
e: Positive charges are sent from the negative to the positive terminal within the source.

q: By Ohm's law, the potential difference across the resistor is $V =$ _____.
e: By Ohm's law, the potential difference across the resistor is $V = IR$.

q: The total work done in moving a unit positive charge round the complete circuit is _____, which is the emf $E$ of the battery.
e: The total work done is $IR + Ir$, which equals the emf $E$.

q: The internal resistance of a battery is represented by the symbol _____.
e: Internal resistance is represented by the lowercase symbol $r$.

q: The emf of a battery is represented by the symbol _____.
e: Electromotive force is represented by the symbol $E$.

q: The work done in moving a unit positive charge from one end to another of the internal resistance $r$ of the battery is _____.
e: The work done across the internal resistance is $Ir$.

q: In an open circuit, the terminal voltage $V$ is related to emf $E$ by the equation $V =$ _____.
e: In an open circuit, no current flows, so $V = E$.

q: When a battery is charging, the terminal voltage $V$ is _____ than its emf $E$.
e: When charging, $V = E + Ir$, so $V$ is greater than $E$.

q: When two or more electromotive sources are connected in series, the resultant emf is the _____ sum of the individual emfs.
e: The resultant emf is the algebraic sum of the individual emfs.

q: In a series aiding arrangement, the currents leaving the batteries are in the _____ direction.
e: In series aiding, currents leave the batteries in the same direction.

q: In series opposing, the resultant emf is the _____ between the individual emfs.
e: In series opposing, the resultant emf is the difference between individual emfs.

q: In a series connection of batteries, the total internal resistance is the _____ of the individual internal resistances.
e: Total internal resistance in series is the sum ($r_1 + r_2$).

q: In parallel connection of batteries, care must be taken that the terminal of the same _____ should be connected together.
e: Terminals of the same polarity must be connected together in parallel.

q: If batteries in parallel are not connected with the same polarity together, batteries may be _____.
e: Incorrect polarity connection in parallel may damage the batteries.

q: For two batteries with equal emfs $E$ and equal internal resistances $r$ connected in parallel, the resultant emf is _____.
e: The resultant emf of identical batteries in parallel is just $E$.

q: For two batteries with equal internal resistances $r$ connected in parallel, the resultant internal resistance is _____.
e: The resultant internal resistance for two equal resistors $r$ in parallel is $r/2$.

q: In a series aiding arrangement, the batteries can be regarded as a single battery having an emf of _____.
e: In series aiding, they act as a single battery with emf $E_1 + E_2$.

q: In series opposing, the total internal resistance of the two batteries is _____.
e: Even in series opposing, the total internal resistance is $r_1 + r_2$.

q: In parallel connection of batteries, the resultant emf of the parallel-combination is just the emf $E$ of a _____ battery.
e: The combination can be regarded as a single battery having an emf $E$.

q: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of _____ through any part of circuit.
e: Electrical energy is associated with the flow of charge.

q: Electrical energy can be generated from sources of emf such as batteries, generators, dynamos and _____ cells.
e: It can be generated from photovoltaic cells among other sources.

q: Electrical energy can be stored in fuel cells, batteries, capacitors and _____.
e: Electrical energy can be stored in inductors.

q: The work done by the battery in taking the charge $Q$ from A to B is transformed into _____ energy in the resistor.
e: The electrical energy is transformed into heat energy in the resistor.

q: Heat energy is produced in a resistor because _____ collide with the atoms in the resistor when they pass through it.
e: Electrons collide with atoms, producing heat energy.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is _____ hour.
e: The practical unit of electrical energy is kilowatt hour (kWh).

q: $1 \text{ kWh}$ is equal to $1000 \text{ W} \times 1 \text{ h}$, which is _____ J.
e: $1 \text{ kWh} = 3.60 \times 10^6 \text{ J}$.

q: Electrical power is the _____ of transfer of electrical energy.
e: Electrical power is the rate of transfer of electrical energy.

q: If 1 joule of electrical energy is transferred in 1 second, the electrical power is 1 _____.
e: 1 joule per second is equal to 1 watt.

q: The unit of electrical power is watt, which is equivalent to _____ per second.
e: Watt is equivalent to joule per second ($J s^{-1}$).

q: If an electric motor is connected to a battery, the electrical energy will be transformed into _____ energy.
e: An electric motor transforms electrical energy into mechanical energy.

q: The electrical energy $W$ produced by the battery is equal to $VIt$, $I^2Rt$, or _____.
e: Electrical energy can also be calculated as $\frac{V^2}{R}t$.

q: The unit of electrical energy kWh stands for _____ hour.
e: kWh stands for kilowatt hour.

q: When electric current passes through a conductor, the electrons are accelerated due to electric _____.
e: Electrons are accelerated due to the electric field.

q: Electrons lose their kinetic energy which appears as _____ energy.
e: The lost kinetic energy appears as heat energy.

q: The electrical energy $W$ is related to the amount of heat $H$ by the equation $W =$ _____.
e: The relationship is given by the equation $W = JH$.

q: In the equation $W = JH$, $J$ is a constant called Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat, which has a value of _____ $\text{J cal}^{-1}$.
e: Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat $J = 4.2 \text{ J cal}^{-1}$.

q: Joule's law states that the amount of heat produced is directly proportional to the _____ of the current.
e: Heat produced is directly proportional to the square of the current.

q: According to Joule's law, heat produced is directly proportional to the value of resistance and the _____ taken by the current.
e: Heat is proportional to the time taken by the current to pass through the resistor.

q: The formula for heat $H$ produced in a resistor in calories is $H =$ _____.
e: The formula for heat in calories is $H = \frac{I^2Rt}{J}$.

q: The formula for heat $H$ using voltage $V$ is $H = \frac{V^2 t}{R \times}$ _____.
e: Using voltage, the heat formula is $H = \frac{V^2 t}{RJ}$.

q: English physicist James Prescott Joule experimentally studied the heating effect of electric current in the year _____.
e: James Prescott Joule studied this effect in 1841.

q: In Joule's law, the constant $J$ is called Joule's mechanical _____ of heat.
e: $J$ is called Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat.

q: Heat energy is produced in the resistor $R$ which acts as a heating _____.
e: The resistor acts as a heating coil in Joule's calorimeter.

q: The formula for heat $H$ using voltage $V$ and current $I$ is $H =$ _____.
e: The formula using $V$ and $I$ is $H = \frac{VIt}{J}$.

q: The heating effect of electric current has special applications in _____ appliances.
e: The heating effect has special applications in domestic appliances.

q: An electric light bulb consists of a glass bulb containing a _____ filament.
e: An electric light bulb contains a tungsten filament.

q: The tungsten filament has a high melting point of approximately _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
e: Tungsten has a high melting point of ~3000 $^\circ\text{C}$.

q: A small amount of _____, an inert gas, is added to the light bulb after the air is removed.
e: Argon, an inert gas, is added to the light bulb.

q: The tungsten filament emits white light at a temperature of _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
e: It emits white light at a temperature of 1800 $^\circ\text{C}$.

q: Because of the inert gas, the light bulb can be used safely up to the temperature _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
e: The inert gas allows safe use up to 2500 $^\circ\text{C}$.

q: The inert gas in a light bulb reduces _____ of the filament.
e: The inert gas reduces evaporation of the filament.

q: In an electric iron, a mica sheet is wound around the _____ wire.
e: Mica is wound around the nichrome wire in an electric iron.

q: Mica is used in electric irons because it is a good electrical _____ and can withstand very high temperature.
e: Mica is a good electrical insulator.

q: The heating element in an electric iron is controlled by a _____ that switches the current on and off.
e: A thermostat controls the heating element by switching the current.

q: An electric iron typically has an electric power of 750 - _____ W.
e: An electric iron has a power rating of 750-1000 W.

q: In an electric stove, a coil of nichrome wire is placed in the groove of the _____ material.
e: The nichrome coil is placed in a heat-resistant material.

q: A fuse is a thin short wire of _____ alloy.
e: A fuse is made of a tin-lead alloy.

q: A fuse is used in electric circuits to prevent electrical appliances from being damaged if _____ current flows through them.
e: Fuses protect appliances from excessive current.

q: The fuse wire is fitted in a glass tube, also known as a _____, or on a porcelain block.
e: The glass tube is also known as a cartridge.

q: When a current greater than its rating flows, the fuse becomes so hot that it will _____ and break the circuit.
e: The fuse melts to break the circuit.

q: For an appliance rated as 700 W or less, a _____ A fuse should be fitted.
e: A 3 A fuse is used for appliances 700 W or less.

q: For appliances above 700 W, a _____ A fuse should be fitted.
e: A 13 A fuse is used for appliances above 700 W.

q: The voltage and the power of a simple light bulb are usually specified as 220 V and _____ W.
e: A simple light bulb is usually specified as 220 V, 60 W.

q: An electric stove has an electrical power ranging from 600 W to _____ W.
e: An electric stove has a power ranging from 600 W to 2000 W.

q: According to Table 10.1, the electrical power of a laptop computer is _____ W.
e: A laptop computer uses 15-45 W.

q: According to Table 10.1, the electrical power of a refrigerator is _____ W.
e: A refrigerator uses 100-250 W.

q: According to Table 10.1, the electrical power of a radio and television receiver is approximately _____ W.
e: A radio and television receiver uses ~150 W.

q: When a fuse melts and breaks the circuit, the current stops flowing and the electrical appliance is not _____.
e: The appliance is not damaged when the fuse breaks the circuit.

q: The heating effect of electric current is used in domestic appliances such as electric stoves, electric cookers, and electric _____.
e: Electric irons use the heating effect of current.

q: An electric kettle changes electrical energy into _____ energy.
e: An electric kettle changes electrical energy into heat energy.

q: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy to provide electrical _____.
e: A battery provides electrical power.

q: An electric heating bag is an example of an appliance that uses the _____ effect of current.
e: An electric heating bag uses the heating effect of current.

q: The combination of mica sheets and nichrome wire in an electric iron is placed on a heavy _____ plate.
e: The combination is placed on a heavy metal plate.

q: In an electric iron, the combination of mica sheets is sandwiched with another _____ plate.
e: It is sandwiched with another metal plate.

q: The position of the nichrome wire in the electric iron is controlled to maintain the selected _____.
e: The thermostat maintains the selected temperature.

q: A small light bulb used in a torch has a power of a few _____.
e: A torch bulb has a power of a few watts.

q: The bulbs used for illuminating airfields have electrical power of the order of _____ W.
e: Airfield bulbs have a power of the order of 5000 W.

q: For an appliance rated as 700 W or less, a 3 A fuse should be _____.
e: A 3 A fuse should be fitted for such appliances.

q: The fuse wire is made of tin-lead alloy because it has a low _____ point.
e: The tin-lead alloy has a low melting point.

q: A 13 A fuse should be fitted for appliances rated above _____ W.
e: A 13 A fuse is for appliances above 700 W.

q: In a circuit with a 3 A fuse and 220 V source, the maximum power which can safely be consumed is _____ W.
e: Maximum power $P = VI = 220 \times 3 = 660 \text{ W}$.

q: The electrical energy consumed by an air conditioner drawing 10 A from a 220 V line is calculated using the formula $P =$ _____.
e: Electrical power is calculated using $P = VI$.
